response.query: What annotation volumes, active‑learning workflow, annotator training, adjudication SOP, and cost/time estimates are needed to reach target inter‑rater reliability for symptom extraction?
response.answer: To achieve target inter-rater reliability for symptom extraction, typically 100-200 annotation volumes are needed, with annotator training and adjudication SOPs, and cost/time estimates vary based on complexity and annotator experience.

results.title: Video Annotation Services | Video Labeling Company
results.content: # Video Annotation Services for AI/ML. Delivering Precise Video Datasets so Your Computer Vision Models Train Faster and Perform Better — at Any Scale. #### Human-in-the-Loop Video Annotation Services for Consistent, Production-Ready Training Datasets. A bounding box that shifts by 2 pixels per frame is invisible at Frame 10, but by Frame 500, your model is learning from labels that no longer correspond to the object they represent. Our video annotation services address this at the pipeline level. We configure AI-assisted pre-labeling using video annotation tools such as CVAT, V7, Labelbox, or Supervisely to handle large volumes of data. Every production failure in a video-based model can be traced back to one of these problems: objects that lose their identity across frames, events without precise temporal boundaries, pixel-level bleed between overlapping objects, skeletal tracking that breaks during complex motion, scenes that change faster than classifiers can follow, or spatial data that does not align between sensors. Our video tagging services are structured around the specific failure mode(s) your AI/ML solution needs to handle.
